# Deploy on Kubernetes with Helm

The chart deploys the agent as a StatefulSet with a persistent volume, an optional PostgreSQL sidecar, and a public ingress with TLS through cert-manager. It is published as an OCI chart next to the image. The provider pages that follow only differ in how you get a cluster, an ingress controller and DNS.

## Goal

An agent at `https://agent.example.com`, admin API reachable only inside the cluster (or publicly in corporation mode), secrets in Kubernetes Secrets, one `helm upgrade` per release.

## Prerequisites

- A cluster with an ingress controller (ingress-nginx or the provider's) and cert-manager with a ClusterIssuer, see the provider pages.
- `helm` 3.8 or later, `kubectl` pointed at the cluster.
- A DNS record for the hostname pointing at the ingress controller's address.

## Steps

### 1. Create the secrets

The chart creates no Secret. Create one with the agent mnemonic and the database password:

```bash
kubectl create namespace agents
kubectl -n agents create secret generic vs-agent-secrets \
  --from-literal=VERANA_ACCOUNT_MNEMONIC="word1 word2 … word24" \
  --from-literal=POSTGRES_PASSWORD="$(openssl rand -base64 24)"
```

### 2. Write the values

```yaml title="values.yaml"
global:
  domain: example.com          # ingress host becomes {{ name }}.{{ domain }}
name: agent                    # -> agent.example.com
replicas: 1

veranaCorporationId: "42"
veranaRpcEndpointUrl: https://rpc.testnet.verana.network
veranaIndexerBaseUrl: https://idx.testnet.verana.network
veranaChainId: vna-testnet-1
agentMode: standalone
trustedEcsEcosystemDids: "did:webvh:…"   # the testnet ECS ecosystem
publicDidMethod: webvh

adminApiAuthMode: internal     # switch to corporation and set adminApiPublicUrl to expose it

database:
  enabled: true
  user: vsagent
  existingSecret: vs-agent-secrets
  secretPwdKey: POSTGRES_PASSWORD

storage:
  size: 2Gi
  storageClassName: <your storage class>

image:
  repository: veranalabs/vs-agent
  tag: "2.0.0"

ingress:
  tlsSecret: agent-example-com-tls
  public:
    enableCors: true

extraEnv:
  - name: VERANA_ACCOUNT_MNEMONIC
    valueFrom:
      secretKeyRef: { name: vs-agent-secrets, key: VERANA_ACCOUNT_MNEMONIC }
  - name: ECS_CLAIMS_SERVICE_NAME
    value: My Service
  - name: ECS_CLAIMS_SERVICE_TYPE
    value: WEB_PORTAL
  - name: ECS_CLAIMS_SERVICE_DESCRIPTION
    value: A verifiable service.
  - name: ECS_CLAIMS_SERVICE_MINIMUM_AGE_REQUIRED
    value: "0"
  - name: ECS_CLAIMS_SERVICE_LOGO_URI
    value: https://agent.example.com/vt/default/logo.svg
  - name: ECS_CLAIMS_SERVICE_TERMS_AND_CONDITIONS_URI
    value: https://agent.example.com/vt/default/terms.html
  - name: ECS_CLAIMS_SERVICE_PRIVACY_POLICY_URI
    value: https://agent.example.com/vt/default/privacy.html
  - name: ECS_CLAIMS_ORG_NAME
    value: Example Company Ltd
  - name: ECS_CLAIMS_ORG_LOGO_URI
    value: https://agent.example.com/vt/default/logo.svg
  - name: ECS_CLAIMS_ORG_REGISTRY_ID
    value: "12345678"
  - name: ECS_CLAIMS_ORG_ADDRESS
    value: 1 Example Street, Example City
  - name: ECS_CLAIMS_ORG_COUNTRY_CODE
    value: CH
```

The chart derives `PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL` from the ingress host. The cert-manager annotation on the ingress requests the certificate named in `ingress.tlsSecret`; add your ClusterIssuer annotation through the chart's ingress values if it is not the default one.

### 3. Install

```bash
helm upgrade --install agent oci://registry-1.docker.io/veranalabs/vs-agent-chart \
  --version 2.0.0 --namespace agents -f values.yaml
kubectl -n agents rollout status statefulset/agent
```

## Verify

```bash
kubectl -n agents port-forward svc/agent 3000:3000 &
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:3000/v2/agent/health/ready
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:3000/v2/agent/info | jq
curl -s https://agent.example.com/.well-known/did.json | jq .id
```

## Operations

- **Upgrade**: bump `image.tag` and `--version`, `helm upgrade`. **Rollback**: `helm rollback agent`.
- **OpenID4VC**: put the configuration file in a Secret and set `openid4vc.existingSecret`; the chart mounts it and sets the location variable.
- **Backups**: the PostgreSQL volume and the agent volume; see [Back up and restore](./102-backup-restore.mdx).
- **Several agents**: one release per agent, each with its own `name`, secrets and corporation id or mode.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Pod pending | No storage class or no node fits the requests | Set `storage.storageClassName`, check node capacity |
| Certificate never ready | ClusterIssuer missing or DNS not propagated | `kubectl describe certificate`, fix the issuer or DNS |
| Public requests reach the admin API and get `403` | A private ingress points at the admin port in internal mode | Remove it, or switch to corporation mode and set the allowlist |
